title: read cache: local FS LRU cache of IPFS blocks for served content
description:
Why: rust-ipfs stores blocks it ingested locally, but per-block overhead (CID lookup, DAG-CBOR decoding, blockstore traversal) adds latency under load. For arbitrary CID fetches (XGET/X-USENET-IPFS-GET/blob download), content may need to be fetched from the IPFS network which is slow and non-deterministic. A local LRU cache in front of the IPFS block store eliminates repeated fetches for hot content. Since CIDs are immutable and content-addressed, cache invalidation is trivially correct — same CID always means same bytes, forever.

What:
Add a configurable on-disk LRU block cache, sitting between the protocol handlers and the IpfsBlockStore trait:
- On get_raw_block(cid): check cache first; on miss, fetch from IPFS and populate cache.
- On put_raw_block(data): write to IPFS, then populate cache with the result.
- Evict LRU entries when either the byte-size limit or entry-count limit is reached.

Configuration (new [cache] section in config):
  [cache]
  path = "/var/cache/usenet-ipfs/blocks"   # directory for cache files
  max_bytes = 10_737_418_240               # max total cache size in bytes (default 10 GiB)
  max_entries = 1_000_000                  # max number of cached blocks (default 1M)
  # If either limit is reached, LRU entries are evicted until both are satisfied.
  # Set max_bytes = 0 or max_entries = 0 to disable the respective limit.
  # Omit [cache] section entirely to disable caching.

Implementation notes:
- Cache files named by CID string (base32) to allow directory listing for recovery.
- A separate SQLite table (or sled/redb) tracks (cid, size_bytes, last_access) for LRU ordering without scanning the directory.
- The cache must survive process restart — entries on disk are valid indefinitely due to CID immutability.
- Thread-safe: multiple reader tasks may access the cache concurrently.
- Apply to all three protocol surfaces: NNTP ARTICLE/XGET, IMAP FETCH/X-USENET-IPFS-GET, JMAP Email/get and blob download.
